results.title: A practical guide for studying human behavior in the lab | Behavior Research Methods | Springer Nature Link
results.content: # A practical guide for studying human behavior in the lab. In the last few decades, the field of neuroscience has witnessed major technological advances that have allowed researchers to measure and control neural activity with great detail. Yet, behavioral experiments in humans remain an essential approach to investigate the mysteries of the mind. Their relatively modest technological and economic requisites make behavioral research an attractive and accessible experimental avenue for neuroscientists with very diverse backgrounds. Here, we aim at providing a practical guide for a steady walk through the workflow of a typical behavioral experiment with human subjects. This primer concerns the design of an experimental protocol, research ethics, and subject care, as well as best practices for data collection, analysis, and sharing. The goal is to provide clear instructions for both beginners and experienced researchers from diverse backgrounds in planning behavioral experiments. ### Why and How to Design Complementary NeuroIS and Behavioral Experiments.

results.title: The Importance of Ethics in Organisations, Their Leaders, and Sustainability
results.content: In this context, ethical leadership plays a crucial role in creating an inclusive organisational culture, strengthening commitment and fostering innovation, all of which are essential for long-term legitimacy and competitiveness ([Roy et al., 2024](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3387/15/9/372#B41-admsci-15-00372); [Carlos et al., 2025](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3387/15/9/372#B6-admsci-15-00372)). The results corroborate earlier studies demonstrating that ethical leadership is positively associated with employees’ voluntary pro-environmental behaviour ([Robertson & Barling, 2013](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3387/15/9/372#B39-admsci-15-00372)), which, in turn, advances broader sustainability outcomes. For instance, ethical leadership has been linked to a 23% reduction in employee turnover ([SHRM, 2020](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3387/15/9/372#B44-admsci-15-00372)), a 21% increase in the adoption of sustainability practices ([Harvard Business Review, 2019](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3387/15/9/372#B14-admsci-15-00372)), and a 16% improvement in organisational productivity ([McKinsey & Company, 2020](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3387/15/9/372#B25-admsci-15-00372)). Moreover, 67% of employees report engaging in voluntary environmental behaviours under the influence of ethical leadership ([Journal of Business Ethics, 2020](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3387/15/9/372#B20-admsci-15-00372)).
